sections.html: Burleigh County sits in south-central North Dakota. Bismarck is the county seat and the biggest city. The 2020 census counted 98,458 residents, and median household income is $88,701. Most homeowners here pay one combined bill that covers the county, a city or township, a school district and a few smaller districts, so the first job for any seller is finding out which district the parcel sits in.

Every parcel falls in a taxing district that pairs a city or township with a school district, and each pairing has its own total mill levy. A mill is one thousandth of a dollar of taxable value. The county's 2025 levy sheet gives these totals for a sample of districts:

  • City of Bismarck: 237.10 mills
  • City of Lincoln: 227.55
  • City of Wing: 204.52
  • City of Regan: 272.08
  • South Wilton: 274.74
  • Menoken (rural district): 109.40
  • Canfield (rural, three listings): 194.61, 153.92 and 153.92

Rural parcels outside any city usually carry lower totals because there is no city levy. Some townships appear more than once on the sheet because they straddle more than one school or fire district. Levy sheets for 2022 through 2025 are posted on the county's taxes and levies page.

The county prepares, collects and distributes the tax, but the County Commission has no say over what cities, townships, schools and other districts levy. Each of those bodies sends its budget to the county auditor by October 10. The levy is simply the money the district needs divided by its taxable valuation.

The Burleigh County Tax Equalization Office oversees valuation of real property across the county. It is at 221 N 5th Street, Bismarck. The mailing address is PO Box 5518, Bismarck, ND 58506, and the phones are (701) 222-6693 and (701) 222-6691.

The office works under North Dakota Century Code chapter 11-10.1 and relies on computer assisted mass appraisal software. Records are refreshed through reappraisal, building permits and review of sales. Once the State Board of Equalization signs off, the office sends certified values to the auditor, who computes the tax. The State Tax Commissioner then runs a sales ratio study to confirm values track the market.

Local assessors do the first valuation. You can look up property outside Bismarck city limits at burleigh.northdakotaassessors.com, and city property on the City of Bismarck's property information page. The yearly timeline looks like this:

  • February 1: the local assessor sets values
  • April: the local board of equalization reviews them
  • June: the county board reviews what the local boards recommend
  • August: the State Board of Equalization reviews the county boards' work
  • October 10: each taxing body sends its budget to the county auditor

Real estate tax is payable in two installments, the first on March 1 and the second on October 15. Pay the whole bill, special assessments included, by February 15 and you get a 5 percent discount on the consolidated tax. The county mails statements each December (state law sets December 26 as the latest date), and mobile home statements follow in January.

DatePenalty on first installment and specialsPenalty on second installment
March 23%n/a
May 16%n/a
July 19%n/a
October 15 or 1612% (Oct. 15)6% (Oct. 16)

Mobile homes run on their own calendar. The first installment is due February 28, and 2 percent penalties start March 1, climbing 2 points on the first of each month through June. The second installment is due June 30, with penalties from July 1 through October. The February 15 discount applies to mobile home tax too.

To get the discount or avoid a penalty, your payment has to arrive or carry a postmark on or before the deadline. The county cannot vouch for USPS or courier delivery times. It guarantees a date stamp only for the drop box or for a payment handed over at the Auditor's Office.

You can pay online, by phone or by mail. The online portal is the county's property search. Find your parcel by address (type as few characters as you can) or by the parcel number printed on your statement. Owner names on the portal come from the latest tax statement.

  • Online, or by phone at 1-800-272-9829 with jurisdiction code 4434. Phone payment needs your property number.
  • E-check costs $3.98 for amounts under $10,000 and $19.92 for $10,000 or more.
  • Credit card works online or by phone only, with a 3.61 percent fee and a $1.52 minimum.
  • By mail to Burleigh County Auditor, PO Box 5518, Bismarck, ND 58506.

If your statement never arrived, call the county treasurer at 701-222-6718. A missing statement does not move the deadline, so ask for a copy as soon as you notice.

There are two routes: an informal appeal through the boards of equalization, or a formal abatement request.

Outside Bismarck, start with the township or city board of equalization, which meets in April. Inside the city, start with the city assessor. If you want a review that goes further, ask the Tax Equalization Office at (701) 222-6693 about meeting dates before the spring cycle begins.

Abatement runs through N.D.C.C. 57-23-04. You file an application with the county auditor on or before November 1 of the year after the tax becomes delinquent. The board of county commissioners can then abate or refund the tax in whole or in part. The abatement application is linked from the Tax Equalization page.

A parcel becomes subject to foreclosure of the tax lien when taxes, specials and penalties go unpaid into the third year. The Auditor/Treasurer tracks these parcels, notifies interested parties and holds an annual sale. A delinquent property list and the sale terms are posted on the county site.

  • Before June 1: foreclosure notice goes to the owner and occupants.
  • Before August 1: notice is published in the county newspaper.
  • October 1: tax lien foreclosure date. Pay in full by 5 p.m.
  • At least 15 days before the sale: notice is posted in the office and online.
  • Third Tuesday of November: the annual tax sale.

Between October 2 and the sale, an owner can still bring the account current by paying all taxes, specials, interest and penalties before the sale starts. For what happens to a parcel after the sale, read the posted sale terms or ask the treasurer.

The Tax Equalization page lists several exemptions. They cover permanent wheelchair confinement, blindness, and paraplegic disabled veterans with VA adaptive housing. There is also a farm residence exemption, and a separate application for new or expanding businesses.

Two credits matter to many owners. The homestead credit is for people 65 or older, or permanently and totally disabled, with income under $70,000. The disabled veteran credit needs an honorable discharge and a VA rating of 50 percent or more.

Filing dates for these credits change from year to year. Call the Tax Equalization Office for the current deadline before relying on any date you find online.

At closing the title company pays current and past taxes out of your proceeds. Ask the county auditor for a payoff figure good through your closing date, because the penalty steps on March 2, May 1, July 1 and October 15 can change the amount.

Special assessments need their own check. If the house is in a city, the city takes those payments and can give you the remaining balance. For rural property, special assessments are paid at the county Auditor/Treasurer's office.

A short checklist before you set a closing date:

  • Get a tax payoff figure from the auditor for the exact closing day.
  • Ask the city or county for any special assessment balance.
  • Pull your mortgage payoff letter.
  • Confirm whether the current year's installment is paid or still open.

We buy Burleigh County houses as-is, including ones with back taxes, so you do not have to catch up the bill before you sell.

faqs.q: Where is the Burleigh County treasurer's office?
faqs.a: It is at 221 N 5th Street, Bismarck, ND 58501. The main phone is 701-222-6718, and the mailing address is PO Box 5518, Bismarck, ND 58506.

faqs.q: How is property tax figured in Burleigh County?
faqs.a: Assessed value is 50 percent of market value. Taxable value is 9 percent of assessed value for residential property and 10 percent for commercial and agricultural property. The consolidated tax is taxable value times the combined mill levy of your taxing districts.

faqs.q: When is the Burleigh County tax sale?
faqs.a: The annual sale is on the third Tuesday of November, for parcels whose tax lien foreclosure date was October 1. You can pay up to the moment the sale begins.

faqs.q: How do I get the 5 percent discount in Burleigh County?
faqs.a: Pay the entire tax, special assessments included, by February 15. Payments received or postmarked after that date get no discount.

faqs.q: Who do I call to dispute my value?
faqs.a: Call the Burleigh County Tax Equalization Office at (701) 222-6693, or your local city or township assessor. For a formal appeal, apply for abatement with the county auditor by November 1 of the year after the tax becomes delinquent.
